question: The interim Government was provisioned under which Plan/Act of the Government of India, by the Britishers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cabinet Mission Plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cabinet Mission Plan was announced in 1946 by the British government to discuss and plan for the transfer of power from British rule to Indian leadership.
 
• It proposed the formation of an interim government that would be responsible for the administration of the country until a new constitution was framed.
 
• The plan also recommended the establishment of a Constituent Assembly to draft the Constitution of India.
 
• The Cabinet Mission consisted of three British Cabinet members: Lord Pethick-Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps, and A.V. Alexander.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cripps Mission Plan**:

 
 
• Proposed in 1942, the Cripps Mission aimed to secure Indian cooperation in World War II by offering limited self-governance.
 
• It proposed an Indian Union with a dominion status post-war, which was rejected by Indian leaders.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935**:
 
 
• The Act provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation and provincial autonomy.
 
• It was the longest act passed by the British Parliament and served as a blueprint for the Constitution of India.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1919**:
 
 
• Also known as Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms, it introduced the dyarchy system in the provinces.
 
• It marked a significant step towards the involvement of Indians in the governance of their country.
